note: Use with nouns and nominal predicates; Japanese usually omits recoverable pronouns.
ja1: 私は学生です。
en1: I am a student.
ja2: 今日は休みです。
en2: Today is a day off.

english: not be a noun; polite negation
note: Formal negative copula; introduce the common conversational contraction as a later variation.
ja1: これは私の傘ではありません。
en1: This is not my umbrella.
ja2: 父は医者ではありません。
en2: My father is not a doctor.

note: Add the question particle to a polite sentence; teach who, what, when and where through vocabulary.
ja1: ここは駅ですか。
en1: Is this the station?
ja2: 何時ですか。
en2: What time is it?

note: The topic particle is pronounced wa; contrast topic with the grammatical subject.
ja1: 私は大阪に住んでいます。
en1: I live in Osaka.
ja2: この店は安いです。
en2: This shop is inexpensive.

note: Use for the answer to a who-or-what question and with existence predicates.
ja1: 誰が来ますか。
en1: Who is coming?
ja2: 妹が来ます。
en2: My younger sister is coming.

note: The object particle is normally pronounced o; it follows the affected object.
ja1: 水を飲みます。
en1: I drink water.
ja2: 本を読みます。
en2: I read a book.

note: The first noun narrows or identifies the second; not all uses express ownership.
ja1: これは母のかばんです。
en1: This is my mother's bag.
ja2: 日本語の先生です。
en2: They are a Japanese-language teacher.

note: Usually replaces the topic or subject particle in elementary affirmative clauses.
ja1: 私も行きます。
en1: I will go too.
ja2: この本も面白いです。
en2: This book is interesting too.

english: at a place where an action happens
note: Contrast action location with the location of existence.
ja1: 図書館で勉強します。
en1: I study at the library.
ja2: 家で昼ご飯を食べます。
en2: I eat lunch at home.

english: an inanimate thing exists at a place
note: Use for things and plants; not the ordinary existence predicate for people or animals.
ja1: 机の上に本があります。
en1: There is a book on the desk.
ja2: 庭に木があります。
en2: There is a tree in the garden.

english: a person or animal exists at a place
note: Use for people and animals; teach location and subject word order together.
ja1: 公園に子供がいます。
en1: There are children in the park.
ja2: 部屋に猫がいます。
en2: There is a cat in the room.

english: go to; move toward a destination
note: The directional particle written he is pronounced e; destination and purpose are distinct.
ja1: 明日、京都へ行きます。
en1: I will go to Kyoto tomorrow.
ja2: 毎日学校に行きます。
en2: I go to school every day.

english: by; using a means or instrument
note: Contrast instrument or transport with action-location uses of the same particle.
ja1: 電車で会社に行きます。
en1: I go to work by train.
ja2: ペンで名前を書きます。
en2: I write my name with a pen.

note: Specific clock times and dates commonly take this particle; relative time words often do not.
ja1: 七時に起きます。
en1: I get up at seven.
ja2: 月曜日に会いましょう。
en2: Let's meet on Monday.

english: from a starting point to an endpoint
note: Use for time or place boundaries; teach that an endpoint need not be a deadline.
ja1: 九時から五時まで働きます。
en1: I work from nine to five.
ja2: 駅から学校まで歩きます。
en2: I walk from the station to the school.

note: Also introduces a companion, but distinguish that function in practice.
ja1: パンと卵を買います。
en1: I will buy bread and eggs.
ja2: 兄と姉がいます。
en2: I have an older brother and an older sister.

english: such things as; a non-exhaustive list
note: The list gives examples rather than claiming to name every item.
ja1: 机の上に本やノートがあります。
en1: There are things such as books and notebooks on the desk.
ja2: りんごやバナナなどを食べます。
en2: I eat fruit such as apples and bananas.

note: Standalone demonstrative pronouns; choose by physical or conversational distance.
ja1: これは新しい時計です。
en1: This is a new watch.
ja2: あれは私の自転車です。
en2: That over there is my bicycle.

english: this noun; that noun; that noun over there
note: These demonstratives require a following noun.
ja1: この道は静かです。
en1: This street is quiet.
ja2: そのかばんは重いですか。
en2: Is that bag heavy?

note: The adjective itself inflects: negative in -kunai and past in -katta; do not attach a plain copula.
ja1: この部屋は広いです。
en1: This room is spacious.
ja2: 昨日は寒かったです。
en2: It was cold yesterday.

note: Use the linking na before nouns, not directly before the polite copula.
ja1: 静かな部屋が好きです。
en1: I like quiet rooms.
ja2: ここは便利な町です。
en2: This is a convenient town.

pattern: Nでした／ではありませんでした
english: was a noun; was not a noun
note: Polite past copula; distinguish noun predicates from adjective and verb inflection.
ja1: 昨日は雨でした。
en1: It was rainy yesterday.
ja2: 先週は休みではありませんでした。
en2: Last week was not a holiday.

note: Can describe a habit or a future event; teach verb groups and dictionary-form lookup together.
ja1: 毎朝走ります。
en1: I run every morning.
ja2: 明日帰ります。
en2: I will return tomorrow.

note: Use for a negative habit or intention; the temporal context determines English tense.
ja1: 私は肉を食べません。
en1: I do not eat meat.
ja2: 今日は出かけません。
en2: I will not go out today.

pattern: 動詞ました／ませんでした
english: polite past verb; polite negative past verb
note: Teach past affirmative and negative as a contrastive pair.
ja1: 昨日映画を見ました。
en1: I watched a film yesterday.
ja2: 今朝は走りませんでした。
en2: I did not run this morning.

note: A direct polite request; appropriateness depends on relationship and burden.
ja1: ここに名前を書いてください。
en1: Please write your name here.
ja2: 少し待ってください。
en2: Please wait a little.

note: At this stage teach ongoing action; resulting states need separate instruction later.
ja1: 今、夕飯を作っています。
en1: I am making dinner now.
ja2: 弟はテレビを見ています。
en2: My younger brother is watching television.

english: may do; it is acceptable to do
note: Requests permission when used as a question; not the same as ability.
ja1: ここに座ってもいいですか。
en1: May I sit here?
ja2: この辞書を使ってもいいです。
en2: You may use this dictionary.

note: Stronger than a preference or suggestion; avoid overusing it with peers.
ja1: ここで写真を撮ってはいけません。
en1: You must not take photographs here.
ja2: この水を飲んではいけません。
en2: You must not drink this water.

note: Requires the plain negative form; scaffold that form before using the request.
ja1: 窓を開けないでください。
en1: Please do not open the window.
ja2: ここで走らないでください。
en2: Please do not run here.

note: Attach to the polite-verb stem; generally states the speaker's desire or asks the listener's.
ja1: 日本に行きたいです。
en1: I want to go to Japan.
ja2: 今日は早く寝たいです。
en2: I want to go to bed early today.

note: Use for the speaker's desire; avoid reporting another person's internal state without evidence.
ja1: 新しい辞書が欲しいです。
en1: I want a new dictionary.
ja2: 何が欲しいですか。
en2: What do you want?

english: would you like to do; invitation
note: A negative question can make an invitation rather than asking about a negative fact.
ja1: 一緒に昼ご飯を食べませんか。
en1: Would you like to have lunch together?
ja2: 週末、映画を見ませんか。
en2: Would you like to watch a film this weekend?

note: Use for joint action; do not translate every instance as a command.
ja1: 駅で会いましょう。
en1: Let's meet at the station.
ja2: 少し休みましょう。
en2: Let's take a short break.

note: The reason precedes the result; a direct explanatory tone is common.
ja1: 寒いですから、窓を閉めます。
en1: I will close the window because it is cold.
ja2: 明日は休みですから、出かけます。
en2: I will go out because tomorrow is a day off.

note: At beginner level teach contrast; later distinguish soft introductory uses.
ja1: この店は小さいですが、便利です。
en1: This shop is small, but it is convenient.
ja2: 行きたいですが、時間がありません。
en2: I want to go, but I do not have time.

note: The verb before this expression stays nonpast even in an account of past events.
ja1: 寝る前に本を読みます。
en1: I read a book before going to bed.
ja2: 食べる前に手を洗います。
en2: I wash my hands before eating.

english: after doing; first do and then
note: The first event must precede the second; teach a practical sequence.
ja1: 宿題をしてから遊びます。
en1: I play after doing my homework.
ja2: 朝ご飯を食べてから出かけました。
en2: I went out after eating breakfast.

english: A is more adjective than B
note: The comparison baseline follows the comparative particle; adjective forms do not become comparative.
ja1: このかばんはあのかばんより軽いです。
en1: This bag is lighter than that bag.
ja2: 今日は昨日より暖かいです。
en2: Today is warmer than yesterday.

english: the most within a stated group
note: Define the comparison set before asking for or asserting a superlative.
ja1: 果物の中でりんごが一番好きです。
en1: Of all fruits, I like apples best.
ja2: この町でどの店が一番安いですか。
en2: Which shop is the cheapest in this town?

english: do something and then do something
note: Conjoins actions; teach te-form sound changes by verb group, including irregular verbs.
ja1: 駅で切符を買って、電車に乗りました。
en1: I bought a ticket at the station and boarded the train.
ja2: 家に帰って、夕飯を作ります。
en2: I will go home and make dinner.

note: Teach common object, person and age counters with their sound changes, not one universal counter.
ja1: りんごを三つ買いました。
en1: I bought three apples.
ja2: 学生が二人います。
en2: There are two students.

english: go in order to do something
note: Attach to the polite-verb stem; motion is part of the meaning.
ja1: 本を借りに図書館へ行きます。
en1: I go to the library to borrow books.
ja2: 友達に会いに行きました。
en2: I went to meet a friend.

english: like a thing; be good at a thing
note: These are adjectival predicates, not transitive verbs; avoid praising one's own skill insensitively.
ja1: 私は音楽が好きです。
en1: I like music.
ja2: 姉は料理が上手です。
en2: My older sister is good at cooking.

note: Sentence-final particles convey stance; tone matters, so do not treat them as interchangeable decoration.
ja1: 今日は暑いですね。
en1: It is hot today, isn't it?
ja2: 次の駅ですよ。
en2: It is the next station, you know.

note: Teach dictionary, negative, past and negative-past verb forms; use appropriate relationships and embedding.
ja1: 明日は家で勉強する。
en1: I will study at home tomorrow.
ja2: 昨日はどこにも行かなかった。
en2: I did not go anywhere yesterday.

note: Choice depends on the following predicate; do not assume complete interchangeability.
ja1: 泳ぐことが好きです。
en1: I like swimming.
ja2: 子供が走っているのを見ました。
en2: I saw a child running.

note: Refers to life experience, not a single dated event; use the plain past form before the nominalizer.
ja1: 富士山に登ったことがあります。
en1: I have climbed Mount Fuji.
ja2: この料理を食べたことがありますか。
en2: Have you ever eaten this dish?

pattern: 動詞たり動詞たりする
english: do things such as; representative actions
note: Lists examples of activities and need not indicate chronological order.
ja1: 休みの日は読んだり散歩したりします。
en1: On days off I do things such as read and take walks.
ja2: 旅行中は泳いだり写真を撮ったりしました。
en2: During the trip I did things such as swim and take photographs.

english: intend to do; intend not to do
note: Represents personal intention; distinguish it from an externally fixed schedule.
ja1: 来年留学するつもりです。
en1: I intend to study abroad next year.
ja2: 今日は外で食べないつもりです。
en2: I intend not to eat out today.

note: Use the dictionary verb or noun plus the possessive linker; plans can involve other people.
ja1: 会議は三時に終わる予定です。
en1: The meeting is scheduled to finish at three.
ja2: 来週は出張の予定です。
en2: I am scheduled to go on a business trip next week.

english: show signs of wanting to do
note: Reports observed desire, commonly of someone other than the speaker.
ja1: 子供は外で遊びたがっています。
en1: The child is showing that they want to play outside.
ja2: 弟は新しいゲームを買いたがっています。
en2: My younger brother wants to buy a new game.

pattern: 動詞語幹／形容詞語幹そうだ
english: look as if; seem about to
note: Appearance-based judgment; teach irregular adjective forms and distinguish hearsay attachment.
ja1: このケーキはおいしそうです。
en1: This cake looks delicious.
ja2: 雨が降りそうです。
en2: It looks as if it will rain.

note: Hearsay follows a complete plain predicate; identify the source when relevant.
ja1: 天気予報によると、明日は晴れるそうです。
en1: According to the weather forecast, it will be sunny tomorrow.
ja2: 田中さんは来月引っ越すそうです。
en2: I hear that Mr. Tanaka is moving next month.

pattern: 普通形ようだ／みたいだ
english: seem; look like; infer from evidence
note: The second form is conversational; noun attachment differs between the two.
ja1: 誰もいないようです。
en1: It seems that no one is here.
ja2: この雲は魚みたいです。
en2: This cloud looks like a fish.

pattern: 動詞辞書形ことができる
note: Explicit ability or possibility; teach before contrasting inflected potential forms.
ja1: ここで切符を買うことができます。
en1: You can buy tickets here.
ja2: 妹は漢字を読むことができます。
en2: My younger sister can read kanji.

note: Teach godan, ichidan and irregular formation; potential forms do not express permission by themselves.
ja1: 私は百メートル泳げます。
en1: I can swim one hundred metres.
ja2: この席から海が見られます。
en2: You can see the sea from this seat.

english: if; when an event has happened
note: Useful for specific conditions and completed-event sequencing; distinguish unreal and actual readings by context.
ja1: 雨が降ったら、家にいます。
en1: If it rains, I will stay home.
ja2: 駅に着いたら、電話してください。
en2: Please call when you arrive at the station.

note: Use with predictable results; avoid freely attaching requests or intentions as results.
ja1: このボタンを押すと、ドアが開きます。
en1: If you press this button, the door opens.
ja2: 春になると、花が咲きます。
en2: When spring comes, flowers bloom.

note: Teach conditional conjugation and restrictions through contrasts with other conditional forms.
ja1: 時間があれば、手伝います。
en1: If I have time, I will help.
ja2: 安ければ、買いたいです。
en2: If it is cheap, I want to buy it.

english: if that is the case; as for a proposed topic
note: Responds to a premise or topic supplied by context rather than just temporal succession.
ja1: 京都に行くなら、秋がいいですよ。
en1: If you are going to Kyoto, autumn is a good time.
ja2: 静かな店なら、駅の前にあります。
en2: If you want a quiet shop, there is one in front of the station.

note: Attach to the verb's te-form, the i-adjective's connective form, or the na-adjective/noun copular connective. The result remains true despite the condition; distinguish concession from permission.
ja1: 雨が降っても、試合はあります。
en1: Even if it rains, the game will take place.
ja2: 忙しくても、朝ご飯を食べます。
en2: Even when I am busy, I eat breakfast.

note: The same person normally performs both actions; the final verb carries the main action.
ja1: 音楽を聞きながら料理します。
en1: I cook while listening to music.
ja2: 歩きながら話しましょう。
en2: Let's talk while walking.

note: Often presents the reason more softly or objectively; nouns and na-adjectives need their linking form.
ja1: 電車が遅れたので、遅刻しました。
en1: I was late because the train was delayed.
ja2: 静かなので、この部屋で勉強します。
en2: I study in this room because it is quiet.

note: Often conveys disappointment or surprise; do not confuse with purpose uses of the same sequence.
ja1: たくさん寝たのに、まだ眠いです。
en1: Although I slept a lot, I am still sleepy.
ja2: この店は高いのに、いつも混んでいます。
en2: Although this shop is expensive, it is always crowded.

english: explanatory framing; the situation is that
note: Connects a statement to context or requests an explanation; not a generic politeness suffix.
ja1: どうして遅れたんですか。
en1: Why were you late?
ja2: 電車が止まったんです。
en2: The train stopped, so that is why.

pattern: 動詞なければならない
note: A double-negative obligation pattern; also teach less formal spoken reductions through listening.
ja1: 明日までに払わなければなりません。
en1: I must pay by tomorrow.
ja2: 今日は早く帰らなければなりません。
en2: I must go home early today.

note: Expresses absence of necessity, not prohibition.
ja1: 今日は来なくてもいいです。
en1: You do not have to come today.
ja2: 全部覚えなくてもいいですよ。
en2: You do not have to memorize everything.

pattern: 動詞た／ないほうがいい
english: had better; should or should not
note: Advice rather than an absolute rule; negative advice uses the nonpast negative.
ja1: 少し休んだほうがいいです。
en1: You should rest a little.
ja2: 夜遅く食べないほうがいいです。
en2: You should not eat late at night.

english: try doing; do as an experiment
note: Describes trying an action to discover its result, not trying unsuccessfully to start it.
ja1: この靴を履いてみます。
en1: I will try these shoes on.
ja2: 日本語で日記を書いてみました。
en2: I tried writing a diary in Japanese.

note: Context distinguishes completion from regret; introduce contractions for recognition later.
ja1: 宿題を全部やってしまいました。
en1: I finished all my homework.
ja2: 財布を忘れてしまいました。
en2: I unfortunately forgot my wallet.

english: do in advance; leave in a state
note: An action prepares for a later need or deliberately maintains a state.
ja1: 旅行の前に切符を買っておきます。
en1: I will buy the tickets before the trip.
ja2: 窓は開けておいてください。
en2: Please leave the window open.

note: Marks outward benefit; avoid using it boastfully toward a senior or recipient.
ja1: 妹に本を読んであげました。
en1: I read a book to my younger sister for her.
ja2: 友達の荷物を持ってあげました。
en2: I carried my friend's luggage for them.

english: someone does a favour for me or my group
note: Subject is the benefactor; the benefit moves toward the speaker's perspective.
ja1: 友達が駅まで送ってくれました。
en1: My friend kindly took me to the station.
ja2: 兄が料理を作ってくれました。
en2: My older brother cooked for me.

note: The beneficiary is normally the topic or subject; the helper is marked as the agent.
ja1: 先生に作文を見てもらいました。
en1: I had my teacher look over my composition.
ja2: 友達に写真を撮ってもらいました。
en2: I had my friend take a photograph.

english: come to do; become able to do
note: Describes a change in ability or habitual behaviour, not a one-off decision.
ja1: 漢字が読めるようになりました。
en1: I have become able to read kanji.
ja2: 毎朝走るようになりました。
en2: I have started running every morning.

note: Foregrounds a personal decision rather than an external arrangement.
ja1: 毎日歩くことにしました。
en1: I decided to walk every day.
ja2: 今日は甘い物を食べないことにします。
en2: I have decided not to eat sweet things today.

english: it is decided; it turns out that
note: Describes an arrangement or outcome without foregrounding the speaker as decision-maker.
ja1: 来月大阪で働くことになりました。
en1: It has been decided that I will work in Osaka next month.
ja2: 会議は来週行うことになりました。
en2: The meeting has been arranged for next week.

english: make an effort to; make a habit of
note: Focuses on deliberate practice, not a completed change of ability.
ja1: 野菜を食べるようにしています。
en1: I make a point of eating vegetables.
ja2: 約束を忘れないようにしてください。
en2: Please make sure not to forget the appointment.

note: Locates an action at its starting boundary; teach alongside ongoing and just-finished versions.
ja1: 今から出かけるところです。
en1: I am just about to go out.
ja2: 昼ご飯を食べるところです。
en2: I am just about to eat lunch.

note: Recency is subjective and can cover more than a few moments.
ja1: この町に来たばかりです。
en1: I have only just arrived in this town.
ja2: 先月この仕事を始めたばかりです。
en2: I only started this job last month.

note: Attach to a verb stem or adjective stem; evaluate against a contextual standard.
ja1: 昨日は食べすぎました。
en1: I ate too much yesterday.
ja2: この靴は小さすぎます。
en2: These shoes are too small.

pattern: 動詞語幹やすい／にくい
english: easy to do; hard to do
note: Describes ease or difficulty of the action, not the actor's ability alone.
ja1: このペンは書きやすいです。
en1: This pen is easy to write with.
ja2: この地図は分かりにくいです。
en2: This map is hard to understand.

english: whether or not; embedded yes-no question
note: Embed a plain question without treating the final predicate as another question particle.
ja1: 店が開いているかどうか知りません。
en1: I do not know whether the shop is open.
ja2: 行けるかどうか、明日連絡します。
en2: I will let you know tomorrow whether I can go.

note: Quote a plain predicate; distinguish speaker opinion from independently verified information.
ja1: 明日は晴れると思います。
en1: I think it will be sunny tomorrow.
ja2: この方法がいいと思います。
en2: I think this method is good.

note: Use plain form for indirect content; distinguish an exact quotation from a paraphrase.
ja1: 先生は明日試験があると言いました。
en1: The teacher said that there would be a test tomorrow.
ja2: 弟は行かないと言っています。
en2: My younger brother says he will not go.

note: Extend the progressive beyond ongoing actions; intransitive change verbs often describe a resulting state.
ja1: 窓が開いています。
en1: The window is open.
ja2: 私は東京に住んでいます。
en2: I live in Tokyo.

english: a state resulting from deliberate action
note: Typically uses a transitive verb and implies that someone arranged the result.
ja1: 机に資料が置いてあります。
en1: The documents have been placed on the desk.
ja2: 壁に地図が貼ってあります。
en2: A map has been put up on the wall.

english: passive voice; be affected by another's action
note: Teach direct passives first and introduce affected-person passives with context.
ja1: 私は先生に褒められました。
en1: I was praised by my teacher.
ja2: この本は多くの人に読まれています。
en2: This book is read by many people.

english: respectful description of someone else's action
note: Raises the subject's action; use an eligible verb stem or verbal noun with its appropriate honorific prefix. Introduce special respectful verbs separately and do not use for oneself.
ja1: 先生はもうお帰りになりました。
en1: The teacher has already gone home.
ja2: 部長は資料をお読みになりました。
en2: The department manager read the documents.

note: Causative meaning depends on context; explicitly distinguish permission from coercion.
ja1: 母は子供に野菜を食べさせました。
en1: The mother made the child eat vegetables.
ja2: 先生は学生に自由に話させました。
en2: The teacher let the students speak freely.

note: Subject experiences imposed action; practise the full form before conversational contractions.
ja1: 私は一時間待たされました。
en1: I was made to wait for an hour.
ja2: 弟は部屋を掃除させられました。
en2: My younger brother was made to clean the room.

english: humble description of one's own action
note: Lowers the speaker's action relative to its respected recipient; does not simply mean formal speech.
ja1: 私が荷物をお持ちします。
en1: I will carry your luggage.
ja2: 会場をご案内します。
en2: I will show you around the venue.

pattern: 動詞ていただけませんか
note: A deferential request for a favour; teach it with realistic recipient and burden choices.
ja1: もう一度説明していただけませんか。
en1: Could you kindly explain it once more?
ja2: この書類を確認していただけませんか。
en2: Could you please check this document?

note: A request for permission to act; distinguish the speaker as actor from causative commands to others.
ja1: 少し考えさせてください。
en1: Please let me think for a moment.
ja2: 私にも手伝わせてください。
en2: Please let me help too.

note: An evidence-based expectation, not moral advice or an absolute guarantee.
ja1: 田中さんはもう駅に着いたはずです。
en1: Mr. Tanaka should have arrived at the station by now.
ja2: 今日は日曜日だから、店は休みのはずです。
en2: Since today is Sunday, the shop should be closed.

english: it does not follow that; not necessarily
note: Partially or generally denies an inference rather than always denying the entire proposition.
ja1: 高い物がいつも良いわけではありません。
en1: Expensive things are not always good.
ja2: 日本語が全部分かるわけではありません。
en2: It is not that I understand all Japanese.

note: Strong subjective denial based on reasoning or conviction.
ja1: 一日で全部覚えられるわけがありません。
en1: There is no way I can memorize everything in one day.
ja2: 彼が約束を忘れるわけがない。
en2: There is no way he would forget his promise.

pattern: 動詞わけにはいかない
english: cannot do because of circumstances or duty
note: Not physical inability; an obligation or social constraint prevents the action.
ja1: 明日は試験なので、休むわけにはいきません。
en1: I cannot take the day off because I have an exam tomorrow.
ja2: 大事な約束を破るわけにはいきません。
en2: I cannot break an important promise.

english: should; ought to as a principle
note: Normative judgment can sound strong; teach negative form and softened advice alternatives.
ja1: 約束は守るべきです。
en1: You should keep your promises.
ja2: 人の話を最後まで聞くべきです。
en2: You should listen to people until they finish.

note: Expresses possibility with less confidence than a prediction stated as certain.
ja1: 夕方は雨になるかもしれません。
en1: It might rain in the evening.
ja2: 彼は道に迷ったかもしれません。
en2: He may have lost his way.

english: must be; surely based on inference
note: Strong inference, not direct evidence or legal obligation.
ja1: 電気がついているから、誰かいるに違いない。
en1: The lights are on, so someone must be there.
ja2: 彼はこの知らせを喜ぶに違いありません。
en2: He will surely be pleased by this news.

note: Distinguish evidential use from the suffix describing typical qualities.
ja1: 駅の近くに新しい店ができたらしいです。
en1: Apparently a new shop has opened near the station.
ja2: 彼は来週帰国するらしいです。
en2: Apparently he will return to his country next week.

english: typical of; characteristic of a noun
note: Expresses a quality fitting an expected type; it is not the evidential use.
ja1: 今日は春らしい天気です。
en1: Today's weather is typical of spring.
ja2: 彼女らしい丁寧な答えでした。
en2: It was a careful answer that was characteristic of her.

english: in order to; for a purpose
note: Usually links a controllable action to its intended purpose; contrast purpose with cause.
ja1: 留学するために貯金しています。
en1: I am saving money in order to study abroad.
ja2: 健康のために毎日歩いています。
en2: I walk every day for my health.

english: so that; in order that a state becomes possible
note: Common with potential and negative predicates; often avoids a directly volitional goal.
ja1: 忘れないようにメモします。
en1: I make a note so that I will not forget.
ja2: 後ろの人にも聞こえるように話してください。
en2: Please speak so that the people at the back can hear too.

note: Take an opportunity before the stated change occurs; teach alongside affirmative while-still uses.
ja1: 雨が降らないうちに帰りましょう。
en1: Let's go home before it rains.
ja2: 忘れないうちに書いておきます。
en2: I will write it down before I forget.

note: The event occurs within the stated interval; contrast an activity maintained throughout the interval.
ja1: 留守の間に荷物が届きました。
en1: A parcel arrived while I was out.
ja2: 日本にいる間に京都を訪れたいです。
en2: I want to visit Kyoto while I am in Japan.

english: while a state lasts; before the opportunity passes
note: A temporary state provides a window for action or gradual change.
ja1: 若いうちに色々な経験をしたいです。
en1: I want to have many experiences while I am young.
ja2: 温かいうちに食べてください。
en2: Please eat it while it is warm.

note: A sudden event follows immediately; usually reports an actual unexpected occurrence.
ja1: 窓を開けたとたんに、風が入ってきました。
en1: The instant I opened the window, wind came in.
ja2: 家を出たとたんに、雨が降り始めました。
en2: Just as I left the house, it began to rain.

note: Describes a recurring pairing of events; attach nouns with a possessive linker.
ja1: この歌を聞くたびに、故郷を思い出します。
en1: Every time I hear this song, I remember my hometown.
ja2: 旅行のたびに写真をたくさん撮ります。
en2: I take many photographs every time I travel.

english: while doing something else; taking the opportunity
note: The secondary action is convenient alongside a primary task.
ja1: 買い物に行くついでに、手紙を出します。
en1: I will post the letter while I am out shopping.
ja2: 散歩のついでに、パンを買いました。
en2: I bought bread while I was out for a walk.

english: leave or remain in a state
note: An earlier action establishes a state that continues during another event.
ja1: 電気をつけたまま寝てしまいました。
en1: I fell asleep with the light left on.
ja2: 靴を履いたまま入らないでください。
en2: Please do not come in with your shoes still on.

note: A written or slightly formal alternative to a negative connective; the irregular verb meaning do uses a special form.
ja1: 朝ご飯を食べずに出かけました。
en1: I went out without eating breakfast.
ja2: 辞書を使わずに読みました。
en2: I read it without using a dictionary.

note: Contrast absence of an accompanying action with causal negative constructions.
ja1: 傘を持たないで出かけました。
en1: I went out without taking an umbrella.
ja2: 今日は外へ行かないで、家で休みます。
en2: Today I will rest at home instead of going out.

english: not as much as; not as adjective as
note: Use a noun as the comparison baseline or a plain clause expressing an expected degree, followed by a negative predicate. Keep the baseline and compared item clear.
ja1: 今日は昨日ほど寒くありません。
en1: Today is not as cold as yesterday.
ja2: この仕事は思ったほど難しくありません。
en2: This job is not as difficult as I expected.

english: to the extent that; so much that
note: An event or quality illustrates the degree of the main description.
ja1: 声が出ないほど驚きました。
en1: I was so surprised that I could not speak.
ja2: 歩けないほど疲れました。
en2: I was so tired that I could not walk.

english: the more one does, the more
note: Requires a repeated predicate or matched adjective forms; teach gradual correlation.
ja1: 読めば読むほど面白くなります。
en1: The more I read, the more interesting it becomes.
ja2: 練習すればするほど上手になります。
en2: The more you practise, the better you become.

note: Coordinate comparable constituents and make the additive relationship explicit.
ja1: 彼は英語だけでなく、中国語も話せます。
en1: He can speak not only English but also Chinese.
ja2: この店は安いだけでなく、サービスもいいです。
en2: This shop is not only inexpensive; its service is good too.

note: Frames a comparison; not necessarily a claim of statistical significance.
ja1: 去年に比べて、今年は暖かいです。
en1: This year is warm compared with last year.
ja2: 電車に比べて、バスは時間がかかります。
en2: The bus takes longer compared with the train.

note: Marks the topic of speaking, thinking or writing rather than a target of an action.
ja1: 日本の歴史について調べています。
en1: I am researching Japanese history.
ja2: 将来について話し合いました。
en2: We discussed the future.

english: toward; with regard to a target
note: Marks an addressee or target of an attitude or action; contrast topical about.
ja1: 先生に対して失礼なことを言ってはいけません。
en1: You must not say rude things to the teacher.
ja2: この計画に対して意見があります。
en2: I have an opinion regarding this plan.

note: Distinguish this variation sense from agency, cause and means.
ja1: 国によって習慣が違います。
en1: Customs differ depending on the country.
ja2: 季節によって値段が変わります。
en2: Prices change depending on the season.

english: by an agent; by means of
note: Formal agency or means; the English translation depends on the predicate.
ja1: この橋は地元の会社によって建てられました。
en1: This bridge was built by a local company.
ja2: 話し合いによって問題を解決しました。
en2: We solved the problem through discussion.

note: Identifies a function, capacity or standpoint rather than similarity.
ja1: 彼は医者として働いています。
en1: He works as a doctor.
ja2: この部屋を会議室として使います。
en2: We use this room as a meeting room.

note: Usually introduces a favourable result; ironic uses require a clear context.
ja1: 先生のおかげで、試験に合格しました。
en1: Thanks to my teacher, I passed the exam.
ja2: 早く予約したおかげで、安く泊まれました。
en2: Thanks to booking early, we were able to stay cheaply.

note: Assigns blame or a negative cause; use carefully when discussing people.
ja1: 雨のせいで、試合が中止になりました。
en1: The game was cancelled because of the rain.
ja2: 寝不足のせいで、集中できません。
en2: I cannot concentrate because of insufficient sleep.

note: The context distinguishes substitution from a compensating trade-off.
ja1: 車で行くかわりに、電車で行きます。
en1: I will go by train instead of going by car.
ja2: 手伝うかわりに、日本語を教えてください。
en2: Please teach me Japanese in exchange for my help.

note: Highlights a surprising minimum or extreme; do not confuse with limitation.
ja1: 忙しくて、昼ご飯を食べる時間さえありません。
en1: I am so busy that I do not even have time to eat lunch.
ja2: 子供でさえ、この問題が解けます。
en2: Even a child can solve this problem.

english: nothing but; only with a negative predicate
note: The restriction requires a negative predicate and often suggests insufficiency.
ja1: 財布には千円しかありません。
en1: I have only one thousand yen in my wallet.
ja2: この店は日曜日しか開いていません。
en2: This shop is open only on Sundays.

note: Often somewhat more formal than the common additive construction; avoid listing unlike constituents.
ja1: 彼女は研究ばかりでなく、教育にも力を入れています。
en1: She puts effort not only into research but also into teaching.
ja2: この町は静かなばかりでなく、交通も便利です。
en2: This town is not only quiet; transport is convenient too.

english: that means; the reported fact is
note: Nominalizes or restates a proposition; explicitly distinguish inference from hearsay in the task.
ja1: つまり、今日は休みということですね。
en1: So that means today is a day off, right?
ja2: 連絡によると、会議は延期ということです。
en2: According to the message, the meeting has been postponed.

english: there is no need to do
note: Reassures against an unnecessary action; not a claim about life experience.
ja1: そんなに心配することはありません。
en1: There is no need to worry so much.
ja2: 急ぐことはありません。
en2: There is no need to hurry.

english: change continuing from now; movement away
note: Teach temporal development separately from literal movement away from the speaker.
ja1: これからも日本語を勉強していきます。
en1: I will continue studying Japanese from now on.
ja2: 鳥が遠くへ飛んでいきました。
en2: The bird flew off into the distance.

english: change up to now; movement toward
note: Marks change reaching the present or movement toward the viewpoint; context determines the sense.
ja1: 少しずつ暖かくなってきました。
en1: It has gradually become warmer.
ja2: 犬がこちらへ走ってきました。
en2: A dog came running toward us.

note: Attach to the verb stem for an intended next action; contrast past narrative immediacy.
ja1: 準備ができ次第、出発します。
en1: We will leave as soon as preparations are complete.
ja2: 結果が分かり次第、ご連絡します。
en2: I will contact you as soon as I know the result.

note: The outcome hinges on the stated variable; distinct from the immediate-sequence construction.
ja1: 天気次第で、予定を変えます。
en1: We will change the plan depending on the weather.
ja2: 努力次第で、結果は変わります。
en2: The result will change depending on the effort.

english: after doing as a prerequisite; upon
note: For temporal use attach the past form; distinguish the context-of-activity sense with nonpast verbs.
ja1: 内容を確認した上で、署名してください。
en1: Please sign after checking the contents.
ja2: 家族と相談した上で、決めました。
en2: I decided after consulting my family.

english: now that; since one has committed
note: A chosen course of action entails responsibility or determination.
ja1: 引き受けた上は、最後までやります。
en1: Now that I have accepted it, I will see it through.
ja2: 参加する上は、規則を守ってください。
en2: If you are going to participate, please follow the rules.

english: now that; since it is the case
note: States a premise followed by an obligation, determination or necessary consequence.
ja1: 約束した以上は、守るべきです。
en1: Now that you have promised, you should keep it.
ja2: 試験を受ける以上は、十分に準備したいです。
en2: Since I am taking the exam, I want to prepare thoroughly.

english: since; now that one has undertaken
note: Emphasizes commitment and a consequent resolve or expectation.
ja1: やるからには、全力を尽くします。
en1: Since I am doing it, I will give it my all.
ja2: 選んだからには、責任を持ちます。
en2: Now that I have chosen it, I will take responsibility.

english: as long as; while a condition holds
note: The result holds within a stated condition or scope; avoid absolute claims beyond that scope.
ja1: 時間がある限り、手伝います。
en1: I will help as long as I have time.
ja2: 私が知っている限り、その店は休みです。
en2: As far as I know, that shop is closed.

note: A necessary condition for changing the result is expressed in the negative clause.
ja1: 雨が降らない限り、出発します。
en1: We will depart unless it rains.
ja2: 本人が来ない限り、手続きはできません。
en2: The procedure cannot be completed unless the person comes in person.

english: be in the process of changing
note: Formal written description of ongoing change; not a general replacement for every progressive.
ja1: 人口は減りつつあります。
en1: The population is declining.
ja2: 状況は改善しつつあります。
en2: The situation is improving.

note: Attach to the verb stem; the concessive reading highlights conflict between awareness and conduct.
ja1: 将来を考えつつ、計画を立てています。
en1: I am making a plan while thinking about the future.
ja2: 悪いと知りつつ、黙っていました。
en2: Although I knew it was wrong, I remained silent.

english: be unable to; find it difficult to
note: Formal inability or reluctance in service and professional contexts; attach to the verb stem.
ja1: その質問にはお答えしかねます。
en1: I am unable to answer that question.
ja2: 今は判断しかねます。
en2: I cannot make a judgment at present.

english: might unfortunately do; could lead to
note: Warns of an undesirable possibility; not the negative of polite inability in ordinary meaning.
ja1: このままでは事故が起こりかねません。
en1: If things continue like this, an accident could happen.
ja2: 無理をすると、体を壊しかねません。
en2: If you overdo it, you could damage your health.

note: Expresses theoretical possibility rather than learned ability; reading varies by conjugated form.
ja1: 誰にでも起こり得る問題です。
en1: It is a problem that could happen to anyone.
ja2: その説明だけでは納得し得ません。
en2: I cannot be convinced by that explanation alone.

note: A formal warning of an undesirable outcome; distinguish an assessed risk from certainty.
ja1: 大雨で川があふれるおそれがあります。
en1: There is a risk that the river will overflow because of heavy rain.
ja2: 交通が乱れるおそれがあります。
en2: There is a risk of transport disruption.

pattern: 普通形に決まっている
note: Strong subjective conviction, often more emphatic than the evidence warrants.
ja1: そんなに安いのには理由があるに決まっています。
en1: There must be a reason it is so cheap.
ja2: 努力したのだから、喜ぶに決まっています。
en2: Of course they will be happy, since they worked hard.

note: Downplays scope or importance; nouns can attach directly.
ja1: これは一つの例にすぎません。
en1: This is merely one example.
ja2: 私は聞いたことを伝えたにすぎません。
en2: I merely passed on what I had heard.

note: Emphatically identifies an essence or cause; primarily formal explanatory style.
ja1: 成功は努力の結果にほかなりません。
en1: The success is nothing other than the result of effort.
ja2: これは信頼の証しにほかなりません。
en2: This is precisely proof of trust.

note: Denies universality, leaving open both positive and negative cases.
ja1: 有名な店がおいしいとは限りません。
en1: A famous restaurant is not necessarily good.
ja2: 早く終わるとは限りません。
en2: It will not necessarily finish early.

english: that explains why; it follows that
note: Arrives at a conclusion from known information, rather than issuing an obligation.
ja1: 五年住んでいたのですか。道に詳しいわけですね。
en1: You lived there for five years? That explains why you know the streets well.
ja2: 一日に十ページなら、十日で百ページ読むわけです。
en2: At ten pages a day, that means reading one hundred pages in ten days.

note: Written-style concession; nouns and na-adjectives generally require the attributive copula.
ja1: 買ったものの、まだ使っていません。
en1: Although I bought it, I have not used it yet.
ja2: 説明を読んだものの、操作は分かりませんでした。
en2: Although I read the explanation, I did not understand how to operate it.

pattern: 普通形にもかかわらず
note: Formal strong contrast between circumstance and outcome; nouns attach directly.
ja1: 雨にもかかわらず、多くの人が来ました。
en1: Despite the rain, many people came.
ja2: 十分に休んだにもかかわらず、疲れが取れません。
en2: Despite resting enough, I cannot shake off my fatigue.

note: Usually conveys blame or contempt; restrict productive practice to appropriate fictional contexts.
ja1: 知っているくせに、教えてくれません。
en1: Even though they know, they will not tell me.
ja2: 約束したくせに、彼は来ませんでした。
en2: Even though he promised, he did not come.

note: An outcome differs from the expectation raised by the first clause.
ja1: この店は高いわりに、量が少ないです。
en1: Considering how expensive this restaurant is, the portions are small.
ja2: 初めてのわりに、上手にできました。
en2: It turned out well considering it was the first attempt.

note: The observed result matches a quality, reputation or invested effort.
ja1: 長く住んでいるだけあって、町に詳しいですね。
en1: As expected of someone who has lived here a long time, you know the town well.
ja2: 人気があるだけあって、この本は面白いです。
en2: As its popularity would suggest, this book is interesting.

note: Adds a stronger or more surprising fact, frequently in formal writing.
ja1: 彼は遅刻したばかりか、資料も忘れました。
en1: He not only arrived late but also forgot the documents.
ja2: この方法は安いばかりか、環境にも優しいです。
en2: This method is not only inexpensive but also environmentally friendly.

note: A formal additive connector; attach to nominal content.
ja1: 英語に加えて、中国語も勉強しています。
en1: In addition to English, I am studying Chinese.
ja2: 雨に加えて、風も強くなりました。
en2: In addition to the rain, the wind grew stronger.

english: starting with; including a representative example
note: The listed item represents a larger group, not necessarily a chronological first step.
ja1: 東京をはじめ、多くの都市で展示会が開かれます。
en1: Exhibitions will be held in many cities, including Tokyo.
ja2: 先生をはじめ、皆さんに感謝しています。
en2: I am grateful to everyone, especially my teacher.

note: Describes duration, geographical reach or a broad range.
ja1: 調査は三年にわたって行われました。
en1: The survey was conducted over three years.
ja2: 広い地域にわたって雨が降りました。
en2: Rain fell throughout a wide area.

note: Distinguish mediation from a whole-period temporal scope.
ja1: 友人を通じて、その会社を知りました。
en1: I learned about that company through a friend.
ja2: 一年を通して暖かい地域です。
en2: It is a region that is warm throughout the year.

note: Formal description of linked developments; correlation need not establish causation.
ja1: 人口の増加に伴って、住宅が増えました。
en1: Housing increased along with population growth.
ja2: 制度の変更に伴って、手続きも変わります。
en2: Procedures will also change with the change in the system.

note: Describes two changes that develop together; usually not an intentional instruction.
ja1: 時間がたつにつれて、不安が減りました。
en1: As time passed, my anxiety diminished.
ja2: 山を登るにつれて、気温が下がります。
en2: As you climb the mountain, the temperature drops.

english: in accordance with; as a change proceeds
note: Teach compliance with a rule separately from correlated progression.
ja1: 説明書に従って組み立ててください。
en1: Please assemble it according to the instructions.
ja2: 年を取るに従って、好みが変わりました。
en2: My tastes changed as I grew older.

english: in response to; according to need
note: The response adapts to the stated condition, scale or requirement.
ja1: 経験に応じて、仕事を分けます。
en1: We allocate work according to experience.
ja2: 必要に応じて、予定を変更できます。
en2: The schedule can be changed as necessary.

english: based on a foundation or evidence
note: Formal grounding in data, a rule or a plan; check that the claimed evidence supports the conclusion.
ja1: 資料に基づいて判断しました。
en1: I made a judgment based on the documents.
ja2: 計画に基づいて工事を進めます。
en2: We will proceed with construction based on the plan.

english: concerning a disputed or discussed issue
note: Often accompanies debate, competition or differing positions.
ja1: 新しい制度をめぐって議論が続いています。
en1: Debate continues over the new system.
ja2: 土地の利用をめぐって意見が分かれました。
en2: Opinions were divided over the use of the land.

note: Formal topic marking; introduce the attributive version for document titles and noun phrases.
ja1: この件に関して、ご質問はありますか。
en1: Do you have any questions regarding this matter?
ja2: 安全に関して詳しく説明します。
en2: I will explain safety matters in detail.

english: on the occasion of; when undertaking
note: A formal significant occasion or planned undertaking, not every routine occurrence.
ja1: 申し込みに際して、身分証明書が必要です。
en1: Identification is required when applying.
ja2: 出発に際して、注意事項を確認しました。
en2: Before departure, we checked the precautions.

note: Formal sequencing of preparation before an event.
ja1: 会議に先立って、資料を配りました。
en1: We distributed documents prior to the meeting.
ja2: 工事に先立って、住民に説明しました。
en2: We explained matters to residents before construction.

english: after a long process; in the end
note: Implies substantial effort, thought or difficulty before an outcome.
ja1: 長く考えた末に、転職を決めました。
en1: After thinking for a long time, I decided to change jobs.
ja2: 話し合った末に、計画を変更しました。
en2: After extensive discussion, we changed the plan.

english: after all that; ultimately an undesirable result
note: Typically describes a negative outcome following effort or indecision.
ja1: 長く待ったあげく、店に入れませんでした。
en1: After waiting a long time, we still could not get into the shop.
ja2: 迷ったあげく、何も買いませんでした。
en2: After much indecision, I bought nothing.

english: ever since; with no subsequent expected action
note: Past verb plus this expression often indicates that an expected next event never happened.
ja1: 彼は出かけたきり、戻ってきません。
en1: He went out and has not returned.
ja2: 去年会ったきり、連絡を取っていません。
en2: We have not been in contact since meeting last year.

note: Signals deliberate omission of an ingredient, participant or consideration.
ja1: 砂糖抜きでコーヒーを飲みます。
en1: I drink coffee without sugar.
ja2: 冗談抜きで、これは大事な問題です。
en2: Joking aside, this is an important issue.

note: Expands beyond a named group; often followed by an additional or broader group.
ja1: 子供に限らず、大人にも人気があります。
en1: It is popular not only with children but also with adults.
ja2: 日本に限らず、世界中で使われています。
en2: It is used not just in Japan but around the world.

note: Formal inclusiveness over a specified criterion; do not imply that every other condition is absent.
ja1: 年齢を問わず参加できます。
en1: People can participate regardless of age.
ja2: 経験の有無を問わず募集しています。
en2: We are recruiting regardless of whether applicants have experience.

english: have no choice but to do
note: Formal unavoidable necessity; the irregular verb meaning do takes a special negative stem.
ja1: 電車が止まったので、歩かざるを得ませんでした。
en1: The trains had stopped, so I had no choice but to walk.
ja2: 費用が足りず、計画を変えざるを得ません。
en2: We lack funds and have no choice but to change the plan.

english: as soon as; no sooner than
note: A rapid actual sequence; literary or formal, with the dictionary form before the connector.
ja1: 彼は席に着くや否や、資料を開きました。
en1: As soon as he sat down, he opened the documents.
ja2: ベルが鳴るや否や、子供たちは外へ走りました。
en2: As soon as the bell rang, the children ran outside.

note: A near-simultaneous sequence, typically describing observed rather than intended actions.
ja1: ドアが開くが早いか、猫が飛び出しました。
en1: No sooner had the door opened than the cat darted out.
ja2: 彼は話を聞くが早いか、電話をかけました。
en2: As soon as he heard the news, he made a phone call.

note: Usually the same subject performs a sudden next action; do not confuse with manner or alternative-list uses.
ja1: 彼は帰宅するなり、ソファに座り込みました。
en1: As soon as he got home, he sank into the sofa.
ja2: 彼女は手紙を読むなり、泣き出しました。
en2: As soon as she read the letter, she began to cry.

note: A recurring action is immediately followed by a result that defeats its purpose.
ja1: 片付けるそばから、子供がおもちゃを出します。
en1: No sooner do I tidy up than the child takes out toys again.
ja2: 覚えたそばから、単語を忘れてしまいます。
en2: I forget words almost as soon as I learn them.

pattern: 動詞てからというもの
english: ever since a major turning point
note: Emphasizes a lasting change beginning with the first event.
ja1: この町に来てからというもの、毎日歩いています。
en1: Ever since moving to this town, I have walked every day.
ja2: 本を出版してからというもの、生活が変わりました。
en2: Ever since publishing the book, my life has changed.

english: once something happens, an inevitable result follows
note: Usually warns of a difficult-to-reverse consequence; not simply a neutral chronological sequence.
ja1: この秘密を話したが最後、もう取り消せません。
en1: Once you reveal this secret, you cannot take it back.
ja2: 彼と議論を始めたが最後、何時間も終わりません。
en2: Once you start arguing with him, it goes on for hours.

english: starting with; an initial event followed by a series
note: Use where the first event launches a succession or expansion.
ja1: 東京公演を皮切りに、全国を回ります。
en1: Starting with the Tokyo performance, they will tour the country.
ja2: 最初の成功を皮切りに、新しい事業が次々に始まりました。
en2: Starting with the first success, new businesses began one after another.

english: as of; by means of, formal
note: Explicitly distinguish formal completion-time use from formal means; teach completion first.
ja1: 本日をもって、受付を終了します。
en1: Applications will close as of today.
ja2: この発表をもって、会議を終わります。
en2: With this presentation, we conclude the meeting.

english: through; after passing through a stage
note: Describes a route or process with meaningful intermediate stages.
ja1: 何度もの話し合いを経て、合意に達しました。
en1: After several rounds of discussion, we reached agreement.
ja2: 大阪を経て、京都に向かいました。
en2: We headed to Kyoto via Osaka.

english: even as far as; down to
note: Emphasizes the farthest extent or finest detail within an inclusive range.
ja1: 服装から話し方に至るまで、よく似ています。
en1: They are very similar, from their clothing right down to their way of speaking.
ja2: 小さな部品に至るまで、確認しました。
en2: We checked everything, down to the smallest parts.

english: when it comes to an extreme case
note: Often singles out a striking example, frequently unfavourable; requires a broader comparison context.
ja1: 皆遅れていましたが、彼に至っては一時間も遅刻しました。
en1: Everyone was late, but he was a full hour late.
ja2: 他の部屋も狭いですが、この部屋に至っては窓さえありません。
en2: The other rooms are small, but this room does not even have a window.

note: Formal consistency with actual circumstances, evidence or an applicable standard.
ja1: 現実に即して、計画を見直す必要があります。
en1: We need to revise the plan in line with reality.
ja2: 事実に即して説明してください。
en2: Please explain in accordance with the facts.

english: in light of; against a standard
note: An evaluative comparison with law, precedent, evidence or criteria.
ja1: 規則に照らして、判断しました。
en1: We made a judgment in light of the rules.
ja2: 過去の例に照らして、この対応は適切です。
en2: In light of past examples, this response is appropriate.

note: Implies that known facts or prior discussion inform the next action.
ja1: 調査結果を踏まえて、対策を考えます。
en1: We will consider measures based on the survey results.
ja2: 前回の反省を踏まえて、方法を変えました。
en2: We changed the method in light of what we learned last time.

note: Formal compliance with a rule, procedure or custom, rather than mere similarity.
ja1: 法律に則って、手続きを進めます。
en1: We will proceed with the procedure in accordance with the law.
ja2: 伝統に則って、式が行われました。
en2: The ceremony was conducted in accordance with tradition.

english: be compelled to; be forced into
note: A formal passive emphasizing external circumstances rather than personal preference.
ja1: 大雪で予定の変更を余儀なくされました。
en1: Heavy snow forced us to change the schedule.
ja2: 工場は操業停止を余儀なくされました。
en2: The factory was forced to suspend operations.

pattern: 動詞ずにはいられない
english: cannot help doing; unable to resist
note: An involuntary feeling or strong inner impulse motivates the action; not externally imposed duty.
ja1: その話を聞くと、笑わずにはいられません。
en1: I cannot help laughing when I hear that story.
ja2: この写真を見ると、故郷を思い出さずにはいられません。
en2: When I see this photograph, I cannot help remembering my hometown.

english: will inevitably cause; be sure to
note: A powerful effect inevitably provokes an action or response; distinguish inner impulse from causal force.
ja1: 彼女の演奏は聴衆を感動させずにはおきません。
en1: Her performance is sure to move the audience.
ja2: この発見は社会の関心を集めずにはおかないでしょう。
en2: This discovery will surely attract public interest.

english: cannot get away without; must do to settle matters
note: A social or practical obligation makes avoidance unacceptable; not a claim of inability.
ja1: 大切な資料をなくしたので、謝らずにはすみません。
en1: Having lost the important documents, I cannot avoid apologizing.
ja2: これほど迷惑をかけた以上、説明せずにはすみません。
en2: After causing this much trouble, I cannot leave without explaining.

pattern: 動詞ないではすまない
note: Negative connective variant of unavoidable accountability; teach as a related but usable construction.
ja1: 約束を破ったのだから、謝らないではすみません。
en1: Since I broke my promise, I cannot avoid apologizing.
ja2: この問題は、責任者が説明しないではすまないでしょう。
en2: The person in charge will have to explain this problem.

english: in order to; with the aim of
note: Formal purpose attached to dictionary form; typically intentional written narration.
ja1: 問題を解決すべく、専門家が集まりました。
en1: Experts gathered in order to solve the problem.
ja2: 真相を確かめるべく、現地へ向かいました。
en2: I headed to the site to establish the truth.

english: in order to; with a firm aim
note: Literary and emphatic purpose; formed from the negative stem and uncommon in ordinary conversation.
ja1: 夢を実現せんがために、努力を重ねました。
en1: I worked persistently in order to realize my dream.
ja2: 技術を学ばんがために、海を渡りました。
en2: They crossed the sea in order to learn the technology.

note: Written notices or maxims; recognize rather than use as routine polite conversation.
ja1: ここに立ち入るべからず。
en1: Do not enter this area.
ja2: 初心を忘れるべからず。
en2: Do not forget your original intentions.

english: unbecoming; something that should never be
note: Attributive condemnation, often attached to a role or professional norm; strongly judgmental.
ja1: 教師にあるまじき発言です。
en1: It is a remark unbecoming of a teacher.
ja2: 責任者にあるまじき態度でした。
en2: It was conduct unbecoming of the person in charge.

note: With perception verbs, the quality makes the experience intolerable; contrast separate emotional-noun use.
ja1: その報告は聞くに堪えない内容でした。
en1: The report's contents were unbearable to hear.
ja2: その映像は見るに堪えませんでした。
en2: The footage was unbearable to watch.

note: Formal emotional expression; distinguish this sense from an unbearable viewing or listening experience.
ja1: 皆様のご支援を賜り、感謝に堪えません。
en1: Having received everyone's support, I am deeply grateful.
ja2: この知らせを聞き、喜びに堪えません。
en2: I am overwhelmed with joy at this news.

note: Attach to a dictionary-form verb or a verbal noun expressing the relevant action. Formal attributive or predicative evaluation; identify what evidence supports the appraisal.
ja1: 彼は信頼に足る人物です。
en1: He is a person worthy of trust.
ja2: 検討に足る提案だと思います。
en2: I think it is a proposal worthy of consideration.

english: cannot bear to do for emotional reasons
note: Compassion or emotional difficulty prevents the action, rather than physical inability.
ja1: この古い手紙は捨てるに忍びません。
en1: I cannot bear to throw away these old letters.
ja2: 彼女の悲しむ姿は見るに忍びません。
en2: I cannot bear to see her looking so sad.

english: even though; even in the case of
note: Formal concession that rejects exemption for a category or circumstance.
ja1: 専門家といえども、間違うことはあります。
en1: Even experts can make mistakes.
ja2: 子供といえども、規則は守る必要があります。
en2: Even children need to follow the rules.

note: Acknowledges a proposition and then qualifies the expected conclusion.
ja1: 春とはいえ、朝はまだ寒いです。
en1: Although it is spring, the mornings are still cold.
ja2: 便利とはいえ、費用がかかりすぎます。
en2: Although it is convenient, it costs too much.

note: Highlights an unrealized better outcome or disappointment; literary or emotionally marked.
ja1: 相談してくれれば、手伝えたものを。
en1: If only you had consulted me, I could have helped.
ja2: 早く出れば間に合ったものを、寝坊してしまいました。
en2: I would have been on time if I had left early, but I overslept.

pattern: (N / V-stem) + ながらに／ながらにして
english: while remaining in a state; from a state
note: Used in fixed state expressions with certain nouns or verb stems; the extended form occurs in established combinations. Do not freely substitute it for the ordinary simultaneous-action connective.
ja1: 彼女は涙ながらに事情を説明しました。
en1: She explained the circumstances in tears.
ja2: このサービスなら、家にいながらにして買い物ができます。
en2: With this service, you can shop without leaving home.

english: unique to; possible only through a special quality
note: Praises or identifies a distinctive strength; typically modifies a noun.
ja1: 地元ならではの料理を楽しみました。
en1: We enjoyed dishes unique to the local area.
ja2: 職人ならではの技術です。
en2: It is skill distinctive to an artisan.

note: Two factors combine to strengthen an outcome rather than simply coexist.
ja1: 努力が才能と相まって、大きな成果を生みました。
en1: Effort combined with talent to produce a major achievement.
ja2: 照明が音楽と相まって、特別な雰囲気を作りました。
en2: The lighting and music together created a special atmosphere.

note: A subject acts contrary to others' concerns or an external situation.
ja1: 周囲の心配をよそに、彼は旅を続けました。
en1: Disregarding the concern of those around him, he continued his journey.
ja2: 不況をよそに、この店は売り上げを伸ばしています。
en2: Despite the recession, this shop is increasing its sales.

note: Depicts determined action despite a substantial obstacle; often admiring in tone.
ja1: 強風をものともせずに、選手たちは走り続けました。
en1: Undaunted by the strong wind, the athletes kept running.
ja2: 困難をものともせずに、研究を続けました。
en2: Undaunted by difficulties, they continued the research.

note: Usually expresses undertaking an action despite illness, opposition or a demanding schedule.
ja1: 彼は病気を押して、会議に出席しました。
en1: He attended the meeting despite being ill.
ja2: 反対を押して、計画を進めました。
en2: They pressed ahead with the plan despite opposition.

note: Highlights neglect of a consideration, which may be courageous or imprudent depending on context.
ja1: 危険を顧みず、救助に向かいました。
en1: They went to help without regard for the danger.
ja2: 家族の心配を顧みず、彼は出発しました。
en2: He departed without regard for his family's concern.

english: depending on; according to the nature of
note: Highly formal expression of dependence, common in institutional decisions.
ja1: 結果いかんで、方針を見直します。
en1: We will revise the policy depending on the results.
ja2: 対応いかんで、信頼を取り戻せるかが決まります。
en2: Whether trust can be regained depends on the response.

pattern: Nのいかんにかかわらず
note: Formal unconditional scope over a specified criterion; frequently used in rules.
ja1: 理由のいかんにかかわらず、無断欠席は認めません。
en1: Unauthorized absence is not permitted regardless of the reason.
ja2: 結果のいかんにかかわらず、報告してください。
en2: Please report regardless of the outcome.

english: both in terms of one aspect and another
note: Lists representative aspects supporting a broad appraisal.
ja1: 色といい形といい、理想的なかばんです。
en1: In both colour and shape, it is an ideal bag.
ja2: 味といい香りといい、すばらしいお茶です。
en2: In both taste and aroma, it is excellent tea.

english: whether one or the other; regardless which
note: Formal paired alternatives with an invariant result.
ja1: 学生であれ社会人であれ、学び続けることは大切です。
en1: Whether one is a student or a working adult, continuing to learn is important.
ja2: 晴天であれ雨天であれ、式は行われます。
en2: Whether the weather is fine or rainy, the ceremony will take place.

english: even if; no matter what one does
note: Volitional-form concession expresses an unchanged outcome or strong resolve.
ja1: 誰が反対しようと、私は意見を変えません。
en1: No matter who objects, I will not change my opinion.
ja2: どれほど時間がかかろうが、最後まで続けます。
en2: No matter how long it takes, I will continue to the end.

english: as if about to; almost to the point of
note: Literary vivid description formed from a negative stem; typically exaggerates an appearance.
ja1: 彼女は泣かんばかりに頼みました。
en1: She pleaded as if she were about to cry.
ja2: 犬は飛びつかんばかりに喜びました。
en2: The dog was so delighted that it seemed ready to jump on me.

note: Literary or formal reason, often used to excuse an unintentional limitation or request understanding.
ja1: 不慣れなこととて、時間がかかってしまいました。
en1: Being unfamiliar with it, I unfortunately took a long time.
ja2: 急なこととて、十分な準備ができませんでした。
en2: Because it was so sudden, we could not prepare adequately.
